query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a controlled amount of Scandium (Sc) into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy will improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of Scandium (Sc) to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: Operating temperatures up to 900°C, corrosion environments, and mechanical loading conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of Sc-based precipitates or solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Scandium is known to form stable precipitates or solid solutions in aluminum and magnesium alloys, which can enhance strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance. The introduction of Sc is expected to refine the microstructure, reduce the formation of stable intermetallic compounds, and improve the overall performance of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (e.g., strength, hardness), enhanced corrosion resistance, and better high-temperature oxidation resistance compared to the as-processed baseline alloy
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.boundary: Density below 6 g/cm3, operating temperatures up to 900°C
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Sc to be added, the exact mechanism of Sc-based precipitates or solid solution strengthening, and the potential interactions between Sc and other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with Sc-containing and Sc-free alloys, subjected to mechanical testing, corrosion testing, and high-temperature oxidation testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sc-containing alloy shows no significant improvement in mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance compared to the Sc-free alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
